item.title: Artificial Intelligence–Enabled Production Systems: Empirical Evidence, Implementation Pipelines, and Industrial Applications
item.content:encoded:
Ruoqi Geng, Cardiff University

Di Li, Warwick University

Yang Cheng, Aalborg University

This special issue addresses how artificial intelligence is becoming embedded in production systems, moving beyond standalone analytics tools to operational capabilities that reshape real-time planning, control, and improvement. The key challenge lies in integrating point solutions—such as deep reinforcement learning for rescheduling or deep learning for predictive maintenance—into reliable end-to-end workflows validated across diverse industrial settings.

The special issue emphasizes empirically grounded research examining the complete AI implementation pipeline in production contexts. This includes business–AI alignment (translating production decisions into AI use cases), data readiness (governance, preparation, and integration), and deployment of AI into operational workflows. The focus is on understanding the enabling and constraining factors—data availability, organisational readiness, and human–AI interaction—that determine whether AI solutions succeed in real production environments.

item.title: Hybrid Human-AI Collaborative Networks
item.content:encoded:
Rosanna Fornasiero, CNR IEIIT

Luis M. Camarinha-Matos, NOVA University Lisbon

Xavier Boucher, Mines Saint-Étienne

Angel Ortiz, Universitat Politècnica de València

Hybrid Collaborative Networks combining human and artificial intelligence actors are becoming fundamental to value creation in digitally distributed ecosystems. These networks integrate diverse actors such as organizations, individuals, intelligent systems, and platforms operating across physical, digital, and organizational boundaries. Understanding their dynamics is essential for ensuring effective design, management, resilience, and sustained performance in changing environments.

This special issue addresses the scientific challenges of managing the life cycle of hybrid human-AI collaborative networks, including how such structures emerge, evolve, adapt, and dissolve. It calls for innovative design methods, adaptive governance models, and frameworks that integrate technological solutions with socio-human and managerial approaches to ensure effective human-AI integration, trust, and scalability.
